text.p: Malaysian Airline System Bhd's (MAS) Malaysia Airlines has begun checking the rudder sections of all its 50 Boeing Co 737 aircraft on the directive of U.S. aviation authorities.

Deputy Transport Minister Wira Mohd Ali Rustam said the examination would be carried out over 10 days using required U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) standards, the national Bernama news agency reported late on Monday.
The rudder checks follow a series of unexplained crashes involving 737 aircraft, including a 1994 USAir crash near Pittsburgh.
Air safety officials in the U.S. have recommended sweeping changes in the "rudder and yaw" control systems of the Boeing 737 to avoid sudden and uncontrolled rolls.
"The check is only a safety measure which will not disrupt the MAS flight schedule," Bernama quoted Wira as saying.
"Aircraft which have been checked and found to be problem free will be allowed to fly as usual. A report on the checks will be sent to the Boeing Co and FAA."
The 737 model comprises about half of the aircraft MAS owns.
